answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may issue claims, then slash that stake when independent, randomly assigned auditors verify fraud. Auditors earn rewards only when their judgments match later evidence, so a swarm of fresh accounts cannot cheaply manufacture trust: each sybil ties up capital, and detected collusion burns it. A whisper of reputation, an ember of activity, or an onyx badge matters only after this costly, auditable track record—not merely because an identity exists.
